newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ethiopia rejects Sudanese charges of aggression.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia rejects Sudanese charges of aggression.

text.p: Ethiopian Foreign Minister Seyoum Mesfin has denied Sudanese charges of aggression as "outrageous and baseless claims."

He was replying, in a letter to the president of the Security Council circulated on Monday, to a recent letter to the council from Sudanese Foreign Minister Ali Osman Mohamed Taha listing a number of alleged "acts of provocation and aggression" by Ethiopia.
"Ethiopia and its defence forces had no role in the military setback suffered by the government of Sudan in its Blue Nile State," Mesfin said.
"Outrageous and baseless claims were made in the letter from the foreign minister of the Sudan which are completely out of character for Ethiopia."

Sudan's latest accusation was "patently aimed at providing an alibi for the military setback visited upon it by the Sudanese People's Liberation Army and its allies," he said, referring to Sudanese anti-government insurgents.

Alluding to an attempt on the life of Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak in Addis Ababa in June 1995, in which Ethiopia says Sudan was implicated, Mesfin added: "If there are rogue states in the world, there is little doubt that the government in Khartoum would top the list."
He also accused the Sudanese representative in Mogadishu of having called last month for a jihad, or holy war, against Ethiopia by Somalis.
The Security Council discussed Sudan's charges of aggression by Ethiopia during closed-door consultations last Wednesday but took no action pending receipt of further information.
